extracted.intended_audience: Operators, compliance officers, and legal/regulatory staff of human drug compounding outsourcing facilities; industry stakeholders interacting with FDA on 503B registration and fees
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements for registering human drug compounding outsourcing facilities under section 503B of the FD&C Act and for complying with associated fee provisions under section 744K. Covers what information must be submitted, reporting schedules and formats, fees (establishment, reinspection), small-business reductions, dispute processes, and related guidance/recordkeeping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual registration window and required registration information
rubrics_metrics.description: Outsourcing facilities must register annually between October 1 and December 31 and provide information including facility name, place of business, a unique facility identifier, and a point of contact's email address and phone number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration must also indicate (1) whether the facility intends to compound, within the next calendar year, a drug on FDA's drug shortage list and (2) whether it compounds from bulk drug substances and, if so, whether it compounds sterile or nonsterile drugs from bulk drug substances. Registered facilities must submit specified drug product reports (see separate metric).

rubrics_metrics.name: Drug product reporting schedule and electronic SPL format
rubrics_metrics.description: Registered outsourcing facilities must submit a drug product report upon initial registration and twice each year (June and December) for products produced during the previous 6-month period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FDA requires these data be submitted electronically, unless a waiver is granted, in structured product labeling (SPL) format. Guidance referenced: 'Providing Regulatory Submissions in Electronic Format—Drug Establishment Registration and Drug Listing' and the eDRLS guidance (sections cited).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory exemptions conditional on meeting 503B requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Drug products compounded in a registered outsourcing facility can qualify for exemptions from (a) FDA approval requirements under section 505, (b) the requirement to label products with adequate directions for use under section 502(f)(1), and (c) certain drug supply chain security requirements under section 582, if the requirements in section 503B are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FDA provides general information and a list of currently registered outsourcing facilities on its website. Meeting the specific statutory and regulatory 503B requirements is the condition for these exemptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment fee assessment and payment requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon registration, facilities are assessed an annual establishment fee and receive an invoice from FDA with instructions for remitting payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Until payment is made for a given fiscal year, an establishment is not considered to be registered as an outsourcing facility. The Fees guidance describes how outsourcing facilities can submit payment and consequences of failure to pay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small business reduction — eligibility, timing, and submission format
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain outsourcing facilities may qualify for a small business reduction in the amount of the annual establishment fee; to qualify, the facility must submit a written request certifying it meets the reduction requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each fiscal year a firm seeks the reduction, it must submit the written request by April 30 of the preceding fiscal year (example: to qualify for FY 2024 reduction, submit by April 30, 2023). The statute requires use of Form FDA 3908 ('Outsourcing Facilities for Human Drug Compounding: Small Business Establishment Fee Reduction Request'). Submit the completed form via email to CDERCollections@fda.hhs.gov. FDA will send a notification letter of its decision and recommends retaining that notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required form and submission channel for small business reduction (Form FDA 3908)
rubrics_metrics.description: The written request for a small business establishment fee reduction must be submitted using Form FDA 3908 in the specified format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form FDA 3908 is available on FDA's website (link provided in the notice). The completed form should be submitted via email to CDERCollections@fda.hhs.gov. Retain FDA's notification letter after submission for recordkeeping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinspection fees — when incurred and invoicing
rubrics_metrics.description: Outsourcing facilities are subject to reinspection fees incurred for each reinspection conducted because of noncompliance identified during a previous inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After a reinspection, FDA will send an invoice to the email address indicated in the facility's registration file; the invoice will contain instructions for remitting the reinspection fee. For more information, FDA directs facilities to its human drug compounding outsourcing facility fees webpage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dispute resolution, reconsideration, and appeal under 21 CFR 10.75
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency regulations at 21 CFR 10.75 provide for internal Agency review of decisions; an outsourcing facility may request reconsideration of an FDA decision related to fee provisions under section 744K and may appeal denials consistent with § 10.75.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for reconsideration should include the facility's rationale that FDA's decision was in error and any additional relevant information. All requests for dispute resolution should be sent via email to the Division of User Fee Management and Budget Formulation at CDERCollections@fda.hhs.gov. If the facility lacks email access, it may mail the request via carrier of its choice; use FDA's website for the most updated physical mailing address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver from electronic submission of registration information
rubrics_metrics.description: A facility may seek a waiver from the electronic submission requirement for registration information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guidance document 'Registration of Human Drug Compounding Outsourcing Facilities Under Section 503B of the FD&C Act (November 2014)' describes the process for electronic submission and how to obtain a waiver. The notice assumes waivers are rare (estimates one per year) and provides an estimated burden for preparing a waiver request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability and role of FDA guidance documents (good guidance practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA has issued guidance documents that (a) describe the process for electronic submission of establishment registration information and waivers, and (b) describe the types and amounts of fees, adjustments required by law, how to submit payment, consequences for failure to pay, and how to qualify as a small business for a fee reduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance titles cited: 'Registration of Human Drug Compounding Outsourcing Facilities Under Section 503B of the FD&C Act (November 2014)' and 'Fees for Human Drug Compounding Outsourcing Facilities Under Sections 503B and 744K of the FD&C Act (November 2014)'. These were issued consistent with FDA's good guidance practice regulations (21 CFR 10.115), which provide for public comment at any time. Links to downloadable guidance are provided in the notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping — retention of small business designation notification
rubrics_metrics.description: Facilities that receive a small business reduction notification should retain a copy of their small business designation notification letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FDA estimates retaining each notification letter requires 30 minutes annually. The notice recommends retaining the notification and uses this retention as part of the estimated recordkeeping burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimated annual reporting and recordkeeping burden (time estimates)
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA provides estimates of the annual respondent and recordkeeping burden (number of respondents, responses per respondent, average burden hours per response) for activities related to registration, waiver requests, fee remission, small business reduction requests, reinspection fees, reconsideration and appeals, and retention of small business notification letters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key estimates from the notice's tables: 79 respondents submitting registrations using SPL at 4.5 hours each (355 total hours); 1 waiver request at 1 hour; 76 fee remissions at 0.5 hours each (38 hours); 18 small business reduction requests at 25 hours each (450 hours); 12 reinspection fee submissions at 0.5 hours each (6 hours); 1 reconsideration and 1 appeal at 1 hour each; recordkeeping for retaining small business letter: 18 recordkeepers at 0.5 hours each (9 hours). These estimates inform planning for compliance burden.
